• Lesson — "Recall-first means list-all: a topic-scoped empty result is not an empty graph"
  hasDescription: Commit 2145d71c95 (tasks/lessons.md). During the M4 bootstrap-skill dry-run, `get_relevant_context` was called with a specific topic, returned "No recorded knowledge relevant to …", and the agent concluded the graph was empty — then recorded decisions that already existed, creating duplicates. Rule: the recall-first step must be a list-all call (`get_relevant_context` with no `topic` parameter). A topic-scoped call returns only records whose embeddings align to that topic; it can silently miss related records that were captured under different framing. List-all is the only safe dedup check before recording. Apply at the start of every capture session and every temporal-bootstrap episode.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>

Searching rdfs:label rather than hasTitle ensures label-only records (no hasTitle) are still found and the title text isn't double-counted. BM25 is raw/corpus-relative — results are ranked and top-k selected rather than filtered by an absolute score. List-all path (no topic → list_instances via SPARQL) is unchanged. Tool remains purely symbolic: no LLM on the retrieval path.

item.text:
`get_relevant_context` is topic-driven by first running a symbolic BM25 search (`entity_index.search_records`) over `rdfs:label` (weighted 2.0) and `hasDescription` (weighted 1.0), then returning the top-k ranked results from the active knowledge graph rather than filtering with an LLM (recorded in **“Rationale: get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)”**).  
When `topic` is not provided, it uses a non-search path (`list_instances` via SPARQL) to list all current records, with `include_history=true` as the only switch to include superseded/deprecated entries.
